note: Public-method parity for the UCT RS QUALITY columns (engineering map 2026-11-08 unit 3-13; plan §12.1; KB 01-methodologies §4), read by tests/test_rs_phase3_parity.py against api/services/relative_strength.clenow_columns. Everything under `published` is transcribed from the reference page (numbers and short facts only); nothing in this file is our own output. The page's worked example is one number chain (a daily exponential-regression slope over a 90-day window, annualised over 260 trading days). It publishes no ticker, no dates, no price series and no R², so the test rebuilds the one series those inputs describe: 90 closes rising exactly 0.05 % a bar (C_k = 100 × 1.0005^k; the 100 start is ours, and the slope of ln C does not depend on it). A pure exponential has R² = 1, so the page's Adjusted Slope equals its annualised slope there. ANNUALISATION: the page uses 260 bars, the product 252 (CLENOW_ANNUALISATION_BARS; the KB notes sources differ, and Quanterlab's re-test uses 252). The page's own convention is checked with the exponent set to 260 for the test; the shipped 252 is checked against the published figure re-based from 260 to 252 bars; and a strict xfail records that the raw 252 figure is NOT within 1 % of 13.88 % (about 3.3 % low), so a change of the exponent cannot slip by.

reference.title: How to find stocks on the move with a better momentum indicator - exponential regression
reference.author: Tim du Toit
reference.transcribed: The worked example's numbers only: window 90 days, daily regression slope 0.05 %, 260 trading days a year, implied one-year increase 13.88 %; and the rule that the Adjusted Slope is the annualised slope multiplied by R².

published.score_rule: adjusted slope = annualised exponential-regression slope × R²
